transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess it’s not anything dramatic, but I’ve been noticing I keep making these little careless mistakes. Like I’ll write the wrong time down on a senior-center class sheet, or I’ll measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I missed the small print or skipped over something. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I know everybody does that sometimes, but it’s been happening enough that I thought maybe I should ask about it.
Does this feel like a change from how careful and attentive you used to be?

Not exactly a change, no. I mean, I’d like to say I used to be more on top of things, but if I’m being honest, even back in elementary school teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books or lose homework. And, uh, I guess I’d stare out the window unless somebody kept me pointed in the right direction. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have these attention and forgetfulness problems caused real trouble for you at work, school, or in daily life?

A little, yes. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has caused some trouble. I’ve stepped back from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops at the center because I was worried I’d mix up instructions or measurements and throw people off. And at home, my wife has started double-checking plans for family visits or center activities so I don’t get the time or details wrong. It’s not a disaster, but… it’s enough that I feel bad about it.
Do you find yourself forgetting conversations or appointments even when you meant to remember them?

Yes… I mean, not constantly, but it does happen. My wife will look right at me and say something simple like, “Dave, the cards are in the hall closet now,” and then a minute later I’m standing there realizing I heard her talking, but I didn’t actually take in where she said they were. It’s not that I’m trying not to listen, if that makes sense.
Before age 12, were you already having these kinds of attention or careless-mistake problems?

Yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad student or anything—I was told I was bright—but even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I forgot my books, or I’d lose homework. And I guess I did stare out the window a fair bit unless someone kept me on track. So… yes, it was there pretty early, I think.
Have these attention and careless-mistake problems been getting noticeably worse over the past few years?

Yes… I suppose it has, though I wouldn’t want to overstate it. It’s been more noticeable since we moved into the condo—about a year and a month ago now. That’s when it started interfering more in a way my wife and I could both see, if that makes sense.
Has anyone close to you told you that your memory or thinking has clearly gotten worse than it used to be?

I’m not sure I’d say “clearly,” no. My wife has pointed out when I miss something she told me or forget where something is, but I don’t think she’s said it like my thinking has really gone downhill or anything. At least… not in those words. Does that answer what you mean?
Has your wife noticed a clear worsening in your memory or thinking compared with how you used to be?

I don’t think she’s noticed a clear worsening, no. She’ll mention little things I miss, but I wouldn’t say she thinks my memory or thinking is really worse than before. At least, that’s my understanding.
Have you yourself noticed a clear decline in your memory or thinking compared with how you used to be?

I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear decline, no. I mean, I have moments where I misplace something or lose track, but compared with how I used to be… I’m not sure I’d call it a real decline. I don’t want to make too much of it if that makes sense.
